issue.title: Include/Exclude Filtering Behavior

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
Currently there is a bug in elasticsearch (https://github.com/elasticsearch/elasticsearch/issues/4047) where empty objects are not stored in `_source` when an include/exclude list is present.

This is because elasticsearch aggressively removes empty objects from the `_source`.

For example, if I have an object

```
{ 'data': { 'key': 'value' } }
```

the following filters will all result in removing `data` from `_source`: `excludes = ['data']`, `excludes = ['data.*']`, `excludes = ['data.key']`, `excludes = ['*.key']`, `includes = ['data.other']`

I believe this behavior is incorrect. I think that we should only remove an object if it is explicitly excluded (`excludes = ['data']`, `excludes = ['data.*']`) or if no elements are included (`includes = ['other_data.*']).  For situations where the object is referenced in an includes list but there is no match, I think the object should remain as an empty object (`includes = ['data.other']`).

This use case makes more sense if we are talking about some nested object that is indexed...

Example:

```
{
  "name": "John Doe",
  "identifiers": {
    "ssn": "987-65-4320",
    "facebook_uid": "12345",
    "twitter_uid": "54321"
  }
```

and `excludes = [ "*.ssn"]` would drop the entire `identifiers` object if the only key was `ssn` for that object, even if we want the empty identifiers object to remain under all circumstances.  We have the same problem with `includes = ["*.instagram_uid"]`.

issue.title: excluding all fields of an object should not remove parent.

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
When excluding '*.f1' from `{ "obj": { "f1": 1, "f2": 2 } }` XContentMapValues.filter returns `{ "obj": { "f2": 2}}`. When run on `{ "obj": { "f1" : 1 }}` we should return `{ "obj": { }}` to maintain object structure. People currently need to always check whether `obj` is there or not.

Closes #4715
Closes #4047
Related to #4491

issue.title: Empty objects are not stored

repository.name: elasticsearch-dsl-py
repository.description: High level Python client for Elasticsearch

issue.body:
While it's possible to store empty objects through the API (cf https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/4047) and the [low level client](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch-py), it's not possible through the `DocType` wrapper.

In addition, empty objects (e.g. stored through the low level client) are removed when updating the doc through its DSL wrapper.

If it's not possible to initialize objects, scripts have to check for the existence of such an object before each access, since it might be still `null`.
